title: Vision Transformer
summary: Turn fixed-size image patches into tokens and run a Transformer encoder over them.
why: Allows global interactions without a convolution at each layer.
interview: Trace patch shapes and compare data efficiency, resolution scaling, and CNN inductive bias.
derivation: The patch projection is equivalent to a convolution with kernel and stride P. At 224x224 and P=16, N=196. Increasing both spatial dimensions by 2 makes N four times larger and dense attention scores sixteen times larger.

steps.note: Require divisible dimensions or explicitly pad/crop.
steps.transformation: unfold P x P non-overlapping patches

steps.note: A strided Conv2d can perform extraction and projection together.
Use CLS output or specify a pooling alternative.

traps: Patch order must agree with positional embedding order.
Changing resolution requires positional handling and changes attention cost.
A plain ViT has weaker locality priors than a CNN; data and pretraining affect the comparison.
tradeoff: Smaller patches preserve spatial detail while increasing token count and attention memory.
code:
import torch
from torch import nn

patch = nn.Conv2d(3, 192, kernel_size=16, stride=16)
x = torch.randn(2, 3, 224, 224)
tokens = patch(x).flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
cls = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, 1, 192))
z = torch.cat((cls.expand(2, -1, -1), tokens), dim=1)
assert z.shape == (2, 197, 192)

variants.title: CNN
variants.flow: image -> local shared kernels -> feature pyramid -> pooled logits
variants.detail: Translation equivariance is approximate once padding, striding, and pooling enter the pipeline.

variants.title: ViT
variants.flow: image -> patches -> global self-attention -> CLS logits
variants.detail: Global token interactions appear immediately; patching still imposes a spatial partition.

figure.title: Dive into Deep Learning
figure.caption: Image patches become token embeddings before Transformer encoding and classification.

explanations.title: From pixels to a classification token
paragraphs: For a 224x224 RGB image and 16x16 patches, the grid contains 14x14=196 patches. Flattening produces [B,196,768] because each patch has 16*16*3 values. A learned projection maps that last dimension to D; it need not equal 768.

Prepend a learned CLS token, yielding [B,197,D], then add learned position embeddings of the same token dimension. Encoder blocks use bidirectional self-attention. A classifier consumes the final CLS representation; other variants pool patch tokens.

Patch projection can be implemented with Conv2d(kernel_size=16,stride=16). It performs local projection; subsequent self-attention connects all patch tokens. For variable-resolution images, patch count and positional embedding handling must be explicit.
explanations.flow:
[B,3,224,224] -> patches [B,196,768]
-> projection [B,196,D] -> prepend CLS [B,197,D]
-> add positions -> encoder stack -> CLS [B,D] -> logits [B,K]

explanations.title: Token count, inductive bias, and resolution cost
paragraphs: A convolution shares a local filter across locations, which builds in locality and approximate translation equivariance subject to stride and boundary effects. A plain ViT has weaker image-specific priors and usually relies more heavily on pretraining and augmentation.

Doubling image height and width quadruples patch count at fixed patch size. The logical attention matrix then has sixteen times as many entries. Flash-style kernels can avoid materializing all entries, but the dense attention arithmetic still grows quadratically in token count.

Smaller patches preserve detail and increase latency and memory. Larger patches reduce tokens and may lose small objects. Classification quality at one resolution does not establish dense prediction quality; detection and segmentation need spatial token features and suitable heads.

explanations.title: Transfer a pretrained ViT without breaking its input contract
paragraphs: Resize or interpolate the two-dimensional grid of positional embeddings when the patch grid changes, treating CLS separately. Match image normalization and channel order used during pretraining. Padding patches should not become unmasked visual evidence.

For dense tasks, discard or supplement the CLS classifier and reshape patch features back into the image grid. A flat ViT is not automatically a multiscale feature pyramid. Compare frozen-backbone probing with full fine-tuning to separate representation quality from adaptation capacity.
